setter.name: Trevor
setter.evidence: I've already heard a few things from him, of course, from the chats that you've had already together

prospect.aka: iPhone (device label used as the speaker name throughout the transcript)
prospect.location: London, UK; also keeps a house in the mountains
prospect.occupation: Art dealer, self-employed, works from home
prospect.training_background: Roughly 28 years of consistent training. Personal trainer twice a week (Tuesday and Thursday, 45 minutes, at 75 pounds per hour), regular swimming, previously a lot of Pilates, long dog walks and bodyweight work at weekends. Uses 12 and 16 kg kettlebells following Trevor's free content.
prospect.medical: Recurring lower back problem that 'freezes'. Injured his back doing kettlebell snatches with too heavy a weight and stopped kettlebells entirely for a period. Currently asymptomatic and training with lighter bells. Also reports sensitivity to air-conditioning draughts triggering back pain.

signals: Already fit and successful: 58, 12.5% body fat described by his own body-composition scan as 'a whole athlete's measurements', self-employed art dealer with a London house, a mountain house and boat holidays.

Explicitly frames the purchase as good-to-best rather than transformation: 'for me, it's less of a transformation... I see it as an additional bonus for me to get better in what I'm doing already good.'

Divergence from the archetype: price was a genuine barrier, not a quality signal — 'That's a lot of money' and 'I wasn't thinking of spending that kind of money'. He is already paying roughly 750 pounds a month for a trainer, so the resistance is to incremental value, not to premium pricing.
Not skeptical_bargain_hunter: he does not shop on price generally and pays a premium for his existing in-person trainer.

goals.text: Stay in shape and keep his muscle mass as he ages
Focus on and strengthen his core
Improve flexibility, which is already decent, to the best it can be
Learn kettlebells properly so he can train anywhere without a gym while travelling
Avoid doing anything that damages his back and stops him training altogether
Keep variety in his routine so he does not get bored and stop
Use exercise to de-stress and keep cognitive function sharp

pains.text: Hurt his lower back doing kettlebell snatches with too heavy a weight and concluded kettlebells were too dangerous for him
Lower back 'freezes' periodically; he links it to work stress and to lifting angry or to prove something
Gets bored quickly and stops anything he does exclusively
Energy is hostage to his working day; he skipped the gym that morning because of unresolved work issues
Anything after roughly 1.30pm is a wasted workout for him, so a missed morning is a missed day
Eats packets of crackers three or four times a week as his one dietary lapse

objections.rep_response: Immediately volunteered a price range instead of holding the number: said price 'can range', 'can also go up to 10' and is 'always around, like, four to six mark'.

objections.raw_quote: Well, I would have to think about it. I'd to go through my finances and see if that would be, you know, viable to do.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it. Later: 'Sounds good. I would say, have think about it. When do you feel like you're going to have that decision for yourself?'

objections.raw_quote: it all depends on my cash flow also, obviously, right now, which is, at the moment, my cash flow is not great, because there's a lot of open invoices that have not been paid, etc.
objections.rep_response: Answered only the mechanics: 'Most people, pay it all in one go, also for, like, their accountability aspect. There is different ways you could do it.' No financial picture was taken.

objections.raw_quote: my trainer, I pay him, I pay him about, I pay much less, you know, I pay him like 75 pounds an hour
objections.rep_response: Reframed it as equivalent — 'It's about the same' — and added 'Trevor is always in your back pocket'.

objections.raw_quote: the point is that I would see that I only would do a workout twice a week with him
objections.rep_response: Conceded the point: 'if you're just looking to have like an extra, then indeed, I wouldn't even per se recommend it a lot.'

objections.raw_quote: when this happens, I think, you know, that , I can't do kettlebells anymore, it's too dangerous and stuff
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged and promised form work: 'so we need to make sure snatches are going to be on point, that you're not going to hurt yourself.' No clinical question was asked.

objections.raw_quote: I'm leaving on the 20th to go for a few weeks to my house in the mountains
objections.rep_response: Asked 'What makes you be like, why not now?' then accommodated by proposing a 24th start date.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No terms given. The rep said only 'Most people, pay it all in one go... There is different ways you could do it. Like, there is nothing written, like, in the stone.'

evidence: Prospect asked for time: 'I'm going to take a few days to think about it and then I can write to Trevor on Instagram, I suppose.'
He committed to reverting: 'give me a few days and I'll revert back.'
No close was attempted; the rep did not ask for the business or send a link.

Counter-evidence: he also asked for written terms — 'Can you send that in writing, the whole conditions and all that, before I go anywhere further?' — the rep said 'Yeah, sure' and never returned to it, so the requested follow-up material was not confirmed.
Counter-evidence: he explicitly framed the offer as an add-on he would not use fully and said he would not drop his existing trainer, which makes conversion unlikely.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to consider for a few days and contact Richard or Trevor. Rep agreed to send written conditions but never confirmed doing so.

notable.note: Three things. First, the rep never held the $6,000 price: within seconds of the first resistance he said 'price can range. It can also go up to 10, but overall, it's always around, like, four to six mark', and later quoted twelve months at 10 rather than the stated 9. Second, the prospect disclosed that kettlebell snatches are what injured his back and the rep proceeded without asking whether anyone had assessed it. Third, a lengthy unrelated third-party conversation in the prospect's office was captured on the recording between 00:36:23 and 00:38:00.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained inversion — the 'iPhone' label carries a large share of the rep's lines and vice versa. Clear examples: 'I'm calling from Bulgaria myself' at 00:00:57 and the whole good-to-best exchange at 00:33:25-00:33:38 are attributed to the wrong speaker. The prospect never states his name; he joined from a device labelled 'iPhone' and the rep addresses him once as 'Sonny' at 00:34:27, which is not corroborated anywhere else and is not recorded as his name.
